Thing is, we should have had arcade quality consoles a lot sooner but it was seen as more lucrative to build inexpensive (inexpensive to build, not inexpensive to buy) stand-up quarter gobblers. The markup on a standup arcade machine was astronomical at the time. They would sell for something like $8,000 - $10,000 USD (adjusting for inflation). That's between 32,000 and 40,000 quarters (not including maintenance and electrical expenses) before your machines start turning a profit. Even assuming your game gets played a lot, you're probably looking at over a year of play time before profit. Many businesses would just lease the machines instead of buying them outright because they were far too expensive.
